title: Trainable Quantum Channels as Computational Primitives for Quantum Learning
authors: Jingwei Wen, Ling Qian, Shijie Wei, Guilu Long
abstract: Variational quantum learning is traditionally constrained to unitary dynamics, often treating quantum channels as detrimental noise. In this work, we reformulate the quantum channels as trainable computational primitives and establish a non-unitary quantum machine learning framework grounded in open-system dynamics. We demonstrate that the outputs of channel-enhanced quantum models form a structured superposition of multiple functional components. Each component is governed by an effective observable whose spectrum can be adaptively modulated during training, a significant departure from the spectral invariance in unitary transformations. Moreover, the proposed framework generalizes conventional unitary quantum models by retaining them as a special case while introducing additional non-unitary degrees of freedom. Furthermore, we reveal that trainable quantum channels enrich the optimization geometry through ensemble-averaged gradient and additional optimization directions induced by the Kraus operators. Empirical evaluations on classification tasks using trainable amplitude-damping and phase-damping channels confirm enhanced optimization dynamics and predictive performance. Our work provides a principled approach for leveraging quantum channels as trainable resources and advances the design of high-performance quantum learning architectures.
summary: The paper proposes a novel Quantum Machine Learning framework by treating dissipative quantum channels (like AD and PD) not as noise, but as trainable computational primitives. By incorporating these non-unitary elements into Variational Quantum Circuits, the model expands its representational space and enriches the optimization landscape. This leads to demonstrably superior training dynamics and predictive performance compared to standard unitary QNNs.
main_problem: Traditional variational quantum learning (QML) is limited to unitary dynamics, ignoring dissipative processes which can be harnessed as computational resources.
main_result: Incorporating trainable quantum channels significantly enhances the optimization geometry of QNNs, leading to faster convergence and better classification accuracy than purely unitary models on benchmark tasks like MNIST.
method: The authors reformulate the model by replacing pure unitaries with parameterized, non-unitary CPTP maps (trainable quantum channels) derived from open-system dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is a Variational Quantum Classifier utilizing trainable Amplitude Damping (AD) and Phase Damping (PD) channels inserted into the variational circuit structure. The model output is a structured superposition of components governed by effective observables.
key_observables: Classification accuracy, training loss reduction rate, and the spectrum of the effective observable ($\lambda$ vs $\phi$, $	heta$).
important_parameters: Channel damping strength ($\phi$), variational circuit parameters ($	heta$), number of qubits (up to 10), and regularization strength ($\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The trainable channels are assumed to be physically realizable CPTP maps, allowing them to introduce adaptive observable geometries beyond unitary constraints.
figures_summary: Figures compare loss/accuracy across different model types (Unitary vs. PD-QNNs vs. AD-QNNs) on MNIST for varying qubit numbers; another figure shows the eigenvalues of the effective observable as a function of channel and unitary parameters.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the framework by contrasting unitary limitations with trainable channels, details the mathematical formulation using Kraus operators and gradient derivations ($\partial_	heta f$ and $\partial_\phi f$), presents empirical results on classification tasks (MNIST/EGSSD), and concludes by summarizing the enhanced optimization dynamics.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses how non-unitary evolution, typically viewed as noise in quantum computation, can be systematically parameterized and utilized to enhance computational power in machine learning algorithms, linking open quantum systems theory to practical QML architectures.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Trainable quantum channels in QNNs. The pa- rameterized quantum channels Eϕ are incorporated into the variational architecture, with the channel parameters ϕ opti- mized jointly with the unitary parameters θ during the train- ing process. The quantum-circuit implementation for the PD and AD channels is realized using an environmental qubit initialized as ρe and controlled operations. The channel pa- rameter is encoded through the controlled rotation Ry(α) ac- cording to the relation ϕ = sin2(α/2).
